title: Baseline, version 0
description: The list of things every repository must have, each stated so that a tool can say whether a repository has it. Written as TOML. Every key is listed here: an unknown key is an error, so a misspelt one fails instead of being ignored.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the baseline follows. A reader that does not know the version must refuse it.

items.description: The items, keyed by id. Keying by id makes a repeated id impossible to write, because TOML rejects a repeated key. At least one.

slug.description: A lower-case slug. An id appears in a report and in an exception, so it is stable and plain.

path.description: A path or glob relative to the repository root, with forward slashes. It may not be absolute and may not contain a `..` segment, so it means the same thing in every checkout and cannot reach outside the repository.

item.description: One thing a repository must have.

title.description: What the item asks for, in words, as a report names it.

kind.description: How the item is checked. `file`: one of some paths exists. `workflow`: a rule holds for the repository's workflows. `setting`: a repository setting on GitHub is on. `ruleset`: a rule holds for the default branch's ruleset.

severity.description: `required`: a repository that lacks it fails the check. `recommended`: it is reported and never fails the check.

applies.description: Limits the item to some repositories. Absent means it applies to every repository.

visibility.description: The item applies only to repositories with one of these visibilities.

source.description: Where the requirement comes from: a link to documentation a person can follow.

check.description: What a tool does to decide whether the repository has it. Its keys depend on `kind`.

file-check.description: Satisfied when at least one of the paths exists.

path_any.description: Paths or globs, relative to the repository root. At least one.

workflow-check.description: Satisfied when a rule holds for every workflow under `.github/workflows`. The rules are a closed list, each defined by the tool that checks it: `actions-pinned`: every action is used at a version or a commit, never at a branch. `permissions-declared`: every workflow states its token permissions. `job-timeouts`: every job states a timeout.

setting-check.description: Satisfied when the named setting is on for the repository on GitHub. The settings are a closed list, each read by the tool that checks it: `secret-scanning`, `secret-scanning-push-protection`, `dependabot-alerts`, `dependabot-security-updates`, `code-scanning`, `delete-branch-on-merge`, and `description` (the repository has one).

ruleset-check.description: Satisfied when a rule holds for an active ruleset that targets the default branch. Classic branch protection does not satisfy it. The rules are a closed list, each defined by the tool that checks it: `pull-request-required`; `approval-required` (at least one approving review); `required-checks-match-answers` (the required status checks include every check the repository names in its baseline answers as `required_checks`); `linear-history`; `no-force-push`; `no-deletion`; `bypass-matches-answers` (who may bypass is what the repository names as `default_branch_bypass`).
